text.p: Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin formed France's new left-wing government on Wednesday comprising 14 full ministers, with Socialist Martine Aubry as number two holding a superministry for employment and social solidarity.

President Jacques Chirac's office announced that Dominique Strauss-Kahn, author of the Socialist party's economic platform in last Sunday's parliamentary election, was appointed minister of economics, finance and industry.
Hubert Vedrine, former chief-of-staff to the late president Francois Mitterrand, was appointed foreign minister and Alain Richard, a Socialist budget expert, will be defence minister.

Socialist Elisabeth Guigou was appointed justice minister, and Jospin's close adviser Claude Allegre, a university professor, minister of education, research and technology. The premier's other closest political associate, Daniel Vaillant, was named minister for relations with parliament.

Jean-Pierre Chevenement, leader of the anti-Maastricht Citizens' Movement, was named interior minister, and Communists Jean-Claude Gayssot and Marie-George Buffet were appointed respectively minister of infrastructure, transport and housing and minister of youth and sports.
Strasbourg mayor Catherine Trautmann will be minister of culture et communications and government spokeswoman and Louis Le Pensec takes charge of agriculture and fisheries. Both are Socialists.

Greens party leader Dominique Voynet was given the environment and regional development ministry and for the centre-left Radical Socialist Party, Emile Zuccarelli will be minister of the civil service, administrative reform and decentralisation.
